yt_posts.topic: TUT came back from the dead, ElizaOS did not: the survival test
yt_posts.engagement_question: Which meme from last cycle comes back first?
yt_posts.body:
Everybody looked at that chart and called it a rug. Down 98%. Dead volume. A profile nobody had posted on in months. Every influencer in your feed will tell you those coins never come back. Then it printed a new all time high...

Here is what actually happened. $TUT on BNB started as a literal tutorial: a developer teaching people how to launch a token, with a demo token deployed on a test network. It became the education meme of the whole chain. My community did a 94x on it last September. Then it went quiet for months and the chart looked like every rug you have ever seen.

This week it went vertical again. Up more than 1,100% in two days into a new all time high, and it became the single most liquidated token in crypto, roughly 42 million wiped out in 24 hours. People shorting a dead meme got obliterated. I sold into the top on the way up and bought back lower, so my bag is bigger now than it was before the run.

Now hold that next to ElizaOS. Formerly ai16z. The third biggest AI token of 2024, behind only TAO and Virtuals. Real product. Real narrative. A genuinely beautiful list of centralized exchange listings. Every single box I check was checked. And on August 5 the founder said the token was completely dead after settling a class action and handing the treasury to the plaintiffs. From a 2.4 billion dollar market cap to basically nothing.

Same category. Opposite outcome. So what actually separated them?

Two things, and neither one is on the chart.

First: are they still posting? Not marketing, posting. A team still showing up daily months after the all time high is still in the game. TUT never stopped. Cooper on the Robinhood chain is doing the same thing right now, climbing with zero marketing.

Second: are they still on centralized exchanges? Listings cost real money to maintain. If a project is still sitting on real exchanges a year after the hype died, somebody is still paying for it. That is a receipt, not a vibe. Watch that list shrink and you are watching the project die in slow motion, which is exactly what is happening to ElizaOS right now.

That is the whole test. Everything else is people arguing about whether last cycle's memes can run again. They can. TUT just proved it, and it proved it in a bear market.

So here is my question: which meme from last cycle comes back first? Drop the ticker in the comments, I read all of them.

And if this changed how you look at a dead looking chart, hit like and subscribe. I would rather you be early on the next one than read about it after.

yt_posts.topic: Bitcoin under the 200-week SMA and the number nobody is pricing in
yt_posts.engagement_question: If you had to bet right now, where does Bitcoin bottom?
yt_posts.body:
Bitcoin is under the 200-week SMA and it is Friday. Two days to reclaim it before the weekly close, or next week gets very red. But there is one number in this market that has never lined up like this before, and almost nobody is talking about it...

First the bad news, because it is real. In 2015, 2019 and 2022 the 200-week SMA marked the bottom, so being under it is not automatically a death sentence; it is where bottoms get made. But it is where they get made, not where they are guaranteed, and right now we are sitting below it going into a weekly close.

The data underneath is red. Retail sales came in negative. Michigan consumer expectations are red. Initial claims came in worse than prior. Layoffs mostly stopped in July, which sounds like good news until you notice almost no new jobs are opening either. That is the version that actually scares me: if something breaks, there is nothing left to replenish it. Meanwhile Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is telling everybody core inflation fell to 2.5% while wages for the bottom 25% of workers rose 5.5%. I do not know a single person who is feeling that.

Then Trump says he will declare the Strait of Hormuz a United States territory. To actually hold that water you need boots on the ground. That is the worst wrench that could get thrown into this machine.

So where is the 40k Bitcoin everybody keeps prophesying? Here is the part people skip. Every previous bear checked three boxes: price went below the previous cycle high, price went at or below the 200-week SMA, and price tagged the 0.786. This cycle we have checked two of the three. The 0.786 is sitting miles lower, down around 40k. Either two boxes were enough this time, or something has to break catastrophically to get the third one.

Now the part nobody is pricing in. ISM manufacturing PMI printed 55.6 in July. Seventh straight month of expansion, the strongest reading since May 2022, and the employment index came back above 50 for the first time in 33 months. Manufacturing is expanding.

Go look at 2024 and 2025. Bitcoin made all time high after all time high while ISM PMI sat in contraction that entire stretch, fighting the macro the whole way.

We have never had economic expansion starting BEFORE the bull run. Not once in the entirety of crypto. Every other time PMI rolled over as the bear started and stayed down. This time it is already climbing while we are still in the drawdown.

So what happens when the thing that spent two years working against us starts working for us instead?

If you had to bet right now, where does Bitcoin bottom? Comment your number, I read all of them.

And if you want to be early on the next one instead of reading about it afterward, hit like and subscribe.

It became the education meme of the whole chain. My community did a 94x on it last September.

Then it went quiet for months and the chart looked like every rug you have ever seen.

This week: up over 1,100% in two days, a new all time high, and roughly 42 million in liquidations in 24 hours.

Now put ElizaOS next to it. Formerly ai16z, the third biggest AI token of 2024 behind TAO and Virtuals.

Real product. Real narrative. A beautiful list of centralized exchanges.

On August 5 the founder called it completely dead.

Same category, opposite outcome. Two things separated them, and neither one is on the chart.

Are they still posting? And are they still paying to stay listed on centralized exchanges?

That is the whole test.

If this changed how you look at a dead looking chart...

x_threads.topic: Bitcoin under the 200-week SMA and the number nobody is pricing in

tweets.text:
Bitcoin is under the 200-week SMA and it is Friday.

Two days to reclaim it before the weekly close.

But there is one number in this market that has never lined up like this before...
tweets.hook: Bitcoin is under the 200-week SMA and it is Friday.

tweets.text:
In 2015, 2019 and 2022 the 200-week SMA marked the bottom.

Being under it is not a death sentence. It is where bottoms get made.

Where they get made, not where they are guaranteed.

The 40k everybody prophesies needs the 0.786.

Every previous bear checked three boxes: below the last cycle high, at or below the 200-week SMA, and the 0.786.

This cycle has checked two.

The jobs picture is the real risk. Layoffs mostly stopped in July, but almost no new jobs are opening either.

If something breaks, there is nothing left to replenish it.

Here is what nobody is pricing in.

ISM manufacturing PMI printed 55.6 in July. Seventh straight month of expansion, strongest since May 2022, employment back above 50 for the first time in 33 months.

In 2024 and 2025 Bitcoin made all time high after all time high while ISM PMI sat in contraction the whole time.

We have never had expansion start BEFORE the bull run. Not once in the entirety of crypto.

If this reframed how you are reading this drawdown...

Follow me for macro and crypto takes that ignore the 4-year cycle echo chamber.

😎
